title: Rolling FT Heuristic vs MILP Active Bench Reconstruction
hypothesis: Deploying the Free Transfer on Antonee Robinson (£4.6m) to extinguish zero-minute risk on departed Barco while promoting João Pedro into a 3-4-3 produces a higher expected floor than rolling 2 FTs for the post-international break window.
methodologyNote: Direct side-by-side simulation comparing heuristic consensus rules (rolling FT into international break) against MILP multi-period dual optimization with a 0.85 discount factor.

arms.name: Template Heuristic (Roll Transfer)
arms.label: Control Arm
arms.tacticalShiftNotes: Preserves 1 FT to hold 2 Free Transfers entering GW4. Leaves Barco (0 projected min) occupying the 3rd bench spot and starts Rogers vs Leicester away.

arms.name: MILP Solver Execution (Robinson + 3-4-3)
arms.label: Counterfactual Treatment
arms.tacticalShiftNotes: Transfers Barco -> Robinson (£4.6m, IPS away) and shifts formation to 3-4-3 promoting in-form João Pedro into the starting XI.

counterfactualFindings: The simulation highlights that the marginal shadow value of saving an extra Free Transfer (+1.92 xP) was insufficient to offset the immediate +4.20 xP security and fixture matchup provided by Robinson, alongside promoting João Pedro (4.60 xP) over Rogers (4.15 xP). The MILP arm captured a net model delta of +3.7 xP while reducing lineup variance from 14.8 to 13.2.
takeaways: Holding deadwood players on the bench degrades effective auto-sub floor equity by 1.84 xP.
The 3-4-3 formation flex unlocked João Pedro's favorable Arsenal transition fixture equity while maintaining Rogers as first auto-sub.
Realised settlement is live/pending official Premier League match completion.
